Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
746 PM EDT Sun Sep 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 247 PM EDT Sunday...

Prolonged dry weather upcoming, with good radiational cooling nights 
leading to areas of frost away from the Champlain Valley starting 
Monday night.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 247 PM EDT Sunday...

1. Rain ending late this afternoon; patchy fog overnight then 
tranquil wx conditions.   

2. High pressure will provide region with dry conditions and 
cool temperatures through most of the week, before the chances of 
showers increase late Friday into next weekend

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 247 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Low-amplitude 850-700mb trough departs ewd this evening 
allowing stratiform rain to taper off quickly. Clearing line has 
already reached the immediate St. Lawrence Valley as of 18 UTC. 
Lingering light rain across central/ern VT should exit east of the 
CT River Valley by 2030 UTC. With wet low-level/soil conditions, it 
appears that patchy dense fog will develop in spots after sunset. 
NAM/HRRR/RRFS model soundings all show a better surge of low-level 
CAA during the pre-dawn hours, and better mixing may yield more low 
stratus as opposed to fog as we head towards daybreak. Either way, 
should see a combination of fog/low clouds helping to keep overnight 
lows mostly in the low-mid 40s areawide. A few 30s are possible in 
the nrn Adirondacks especially around KSLK. Winds will also 
pick up on Lake Champlain out of the north late (see Marine 
section below). 

Large area of high pressure building esewd from northern Ontario 
will then be our controlling weather feature Mon-Thu. Low clouds 
gradually clear on Monday with increasing large-scale subsidence, 
leading toward crisp fall like conditions through the remainder of 
the short term forecast period with PoPs NIL. Looking for highs in 
the upper 50s to lower 60s on Monday, then generally low-mid 60s for 
Tuesday and Wednesday. Overnight lows in the 30s to lower 40s with 
good radiational cooling conditions expected. Look for some patchy 
frost away from the Champlain Valley Monday and Tuesday night...and 
locally widespread frost in the northern Adirondacks and Vermont's 
Northeast Kingdom.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Guidance is in good agreement through late week with 
regards to large high pres anchored over southern Canada and keeping 
our fa dry. However, a large spread begins to develop Friday into 
next weekend with regards to evolution and track of coastal low 
pres, and potential impacts to our cwa. Attm WPC continues to keep 
chc pops into the fcst for late Friday into next weekend, with 
highest probabilities acrs central/eastern VT and <10% near the 
International Border. Initially, deep dry layer in place with pw 
values btwn 0.20 to 0.40" wl produce sunny conditions on Thurs with 
seasonably cool temps. Highs generally in the upper 50s to mid/upper 
60s Thurs/Friday with lows mid 30s to mid 40s. It should be noted, 
the lows fcsted by WPC, especially Weds and Thurs nights are too 
warm, given MEX at SLK is 24F and 28F, while WPC has 34F and 33F. 
Similar scenario is noted acrs central/northern and eastern VT, 
where daily frost advisories will probably be required, given the 
favorable setup for cool night time. As clouds and moisture slowly 
advect back into our cwa by next week, daily low temps warm back 
into the 40s, but cooler daytime highs with northerly flow are 
possible by next weekend. The bottom line is we are not expecting 
any widespread hazardous or significant weather late week into next 
weekend attm.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 00Z Tuesday...A wide range in flight conditions
continues this evening from IFR at BTV to MVFR at 
MPV/RUT/EFK and VFR at MSS/SLK/PBG. Expecting variable 
conditions with the onset of some fog/br and associated 
IFR/LIFR to occur pretty quickly, given recent rainfall and 
light winds. However, a secondary cold front pushes across our 
region between 06z-09z, expect areas of fog/br to transition 
into IFR cigs with MVFR vis, as low level stratus develops under
blocked flow and low level northerly flow. Highest probability 
(60-70%) of long duration 8-14 hours)of IFR/LIFR is at 
SLK/MPV/RUT, with medium confidence (40-60%) at BTV/EFK and 
intervals of IFR or lower conditions possible at MSS/PBG. 
Greatest potential for fog at most sites will be between 02-08z 
this evening, with more stratus likely after 08z, especially 
mountain sites and east side of CPV. Conditions are slowly 
improving to MVFR by 15z and mostly VFR by 18z Monday. 
South/southeast winds become light this evening and shift to the
north/northwest after 06z tonight and increase 5 to 10 knots by
sunrise. 

Outlook...

Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 247 PM EDT Sunday...Near Lake Wind Advisory criteria will be in
place around sunrise on Monday with increasing over-lake lapse 
rates bolstered by northerly gradient flow and low-level cold 
air advection. North winds generally 15-20 kts, but a few gusts 
to 25 kts are possible, especially across the central and 
southern portion of the broad lake and down towards Diamond 
Island. Wave heights in this region should reach 2-3 feet 
between 11-16 UTC before subsiding Monday aftn.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
